title: Dense FP16 2SM：TMEM生命周期的actor化偏序与状态

semantics.event_anchors: enter/return range over selected thread invocations; effect uses its explicit anchor_quantifier (per-thread contribution or one local warp operation). Never collapse two CTA actors or treat all anchors as one family-wide timestamp.
semantics.barrier_join: A dependency into wait.return requires all contributions named by join; a single thread arrival is insufficient.
semantics.liveness: No bounded completion, scheduling fairness or observed GPU execution claimed.
semantics.pair_independence: No order between the two pair lifetimes is asserted. Cluster initialization remains a shared prerequisite, not an invented pair0-before-pair1 order.

composition.temporal_constraints: Only quantified partial_order. Flattening a pointwise edge to all-to-all is invalid.
composition.state_projection: Resource states are logical summaries derived from quantified historical anchor facts; they do not add event order.
composition.acceptance: A completed lifetime claim additionally requires every applicable validity_rule all_of. Mere DAG acyclicity or a local free operation is insufficient.
composition.operation_mapping: alloc/free effect is one local warp operation with32 participating thread invocations, not32 independent resource stores/frees and not one merged peer-pair event.

evidence.claim: alloc may block when capacity is unavailable and stores the allocated address in shared memory; the store is weak. The source comment does not establish non-blocking behavior.
After relinquish_alloc_permit, that CTA may not allocate again. This operation is distinct from deallocation.
For cta_group::2, one warp from each peer CTA must participate while the peer is active. sync describes warp convergence, not a replacement for the caller peer-lifetime handshake.

Allocation-related shared accesses preserve same-address ordering against non-tcgen05 instructions. This constrains the allocated-address write and later same-address observations, not a generic write-effect equals API-return rule.
